Let me analyze this OIML certificate carefully.

This is an OIML Certificate for water meters, issued by LNE (France), under scheme A.

Certificate number: R49/2013-A-FR2-23.03 rev.0
Scheme: A
Issued on March 28th, 2023
Member State: FRANCE
Issuing authority: Laboratoire National de Métrologie et d'Essais (LNE)
Person responsible: Emeric MOREL, Head of Instrumentation Certification Department
Applicant: DIEHL METERING GMBH, Industriestrasse 13, 91522 Ansbach, Germany
Manufacturer: DIEHL METERING GMBH, Industriestrasse 13, 91522 Ansbach, Germany
Certified type: Water meter type 174
Recommendation: R49/2013 (Water meters for cold potable water and hot water)
Annex: 7 pages

The annex (pages 2-8, labeled Page 1/7 through 7/7) contains tables of characteristics for multiple nominal diameters: 50, 65, 80, 100, 125, 150, 200 mm.

Each diameter variant has its own characteristics:

**DN50:**
- Indicating device: Plastic
- Body: Iron cast coated / Stainless steel
- Nominal Diameter: 50 mm
- Connections: Flange DN50 / Rotable flange DN50
- Lengths: 200 mm; 270 mm; 300 mm
- Q3: 25 m³/h
- Q4: 31.25 m³/h
- Temperature ranges: 0.1 to 30 / 0.1 to 50 / 0.1 to 70 / 0.1 to 90 °C
- Q3/Q1 Horizontal: for T30: 40..1000; T50: 40..800; T70: 40..630; T90: 40..400
- Q3/Q1 Vertical etc: T30: 40..800; T50: 40..250; T70: 40..200; T90: 40..160
- Q2/Q1: 1.6
- MAP: 10/16 bar
- Pressure loss class: Δp16
- Indicating range: 99999 m³
- Verification scale interval: 0.01 dm³
- Accuracy class: 2
- Environmental class: B / O
- Climatic influence class: -25°C…55°C
- Electromagnetic influence class: E1 / E2
- Reverse flow: No...
- Software identification: 001.000.008; Checksum CRC: 0h1003

**DN65:**
- Nominal Diameter: 65 mm
- Connections: Flange DN65 / Rotable flange DN65
- Lengths: 200 mm; 300 mm
- Q3: 40 m³/h
- Q4: 50 m³/h
- Same temp ranges
- Q3/Q1 Horizontal: T30: 40..1000; T50: 40..800; T70: 40..630; T90: 40..400
- Q3/Q1 Vertical: T30: 40..800; T50: 40..250; T70: 40..200; T90: 40..160
- Indicating range: 99999 m³
- VSI: 0.01 dm³
- rest same

**DN80:**
- Nominal Diameter: 80 mm
- Connections: Flange DN80 / Rotable flange DN80
- Lengths: 200 mm; 225 mm; 300 mm; 350 mm
- Q3: 63 m³/h
- Q4: 78.75 m³/h
- Indicating range: 999999 m³
- VSI: 0.1 dm³
- rest same

**DN100:**
- Nominal Diameter: 100 mm
- Connections: Flange DN100 / Rotable flange DN100
- Lengths: 250 mm; 350 mm; 360 mm
- Q3: 100 m³/h
- Q4: 125 m³/h
- Indicating range: 999999 m³
- VSI: 0.1 dm³

**DN125:**
- Nominal Diameter: 125 mm
- Connections: Flange DN125
- Lengths: 250 mm
- Q3: 160 m³/h
- Q4: 200 m³/h
- Indicating range: 999999 m³
- VSI: 0.1 dm³

**DN150:**
- Nominal Diameter: 150 mm
- Connections: Flange DN150
- Lengths: 300 mm; 500 mm
- Q3: 250 m³/h
- Q4: 312.5 m³/h
- Temperature ranges: only 0.1 to 30 and 0.1 to 50
- Q3/Q1 Horizontal: T30: 40..1000; T50: 40..800
- Q3/Q1 Vertical: T30: 40..800; T50: 40..250
- Indicating range: 999999 m³
- VSI: 0.1 dm³

**DN200:**
- Nominal Diameter: 200 mm
- Connections: Flange DN200
- Lengths: 350 mm
- Q3: 400 m³/h
- Q4: 500 m³/h
- Temperature ranges: only 0.1 to 30 and 0.1 to 50
- Q3/Q1 Horizontal: T30: 40..1000; T50: 40..800
- Q3/Q1 Vertical: T30: 40..800; T50: 40..250
- Indicating range: 999999 m³
- VSI: 0.1 dm³

So this is a model family with 7 variants (by nominal diameter). The models would be DN50, DN65, DN80, DN100, DN125, DN150, DN200.

Type designation: "174" (water meter type 174).

OIML R 49 evaluation report (LNE): P229560-3 — this could be a test report ID.

Now let me build the JSON.

certificate:
- number: "R49/2013-A-FR2-23.03 rev.0" — should I include "rev.0"? The number as printed: "N° R49/2013-A-FR2-23.03 rev.0". I'll use "R49/2013-A-FR2-23.03 rev.0" or maybe "R49/2013-A-FR2-23.03". Let me keep the full "R49/2013-A-FR2-23.03 rev.0" — hmm. Actually the revision might go to revision_history. The number is "R49/2013-A-FR2-23.03" and revision 0. I'll include the number as "R49/2013-A-FR2-23.03" and add revision_history entry: revision "0", date 2023-03-28, changes null (or "Initial issue"). Actually the change is not stated, so maybe leave changes null or omit. The schema says revision "0" string, date, changes. Since rev.0 with no stated changes, I could put changes: "Initial issue". But rule 8 says don't fabricate. Hmm, "rev.0" implies initial. I'll put "Initial issue" — that's a reasonable interpretation, but it's fabrication. Better to omit changes or set null. The schema example shows revision, date, changes. I'll include changes: null? Actually better to just omit the field if not present. Hmm, but rev 0 is the initial revision. I'll set changes: "Initial issue" — risky. Let me just leave it null. Actually schema says `revision (string, e.g. "0" not 0), date, changes`. I'll include with changes: null.

- scheme: "A"
- project_number: maybe from evaluation report "P229560-3"? The evaluation report is "OIML R 49 EVALUATION REPORT (LNE) : P229560-3". That's the report ID. project_number could be P229560-3? I think that's reasonable — but the schema has project_number field; the LNE reference "38973 rév. n°0" is the LNE internal form reference. Hmm. "Référence LNE - 38973 rév. n°0" is a document reference of the certificate form. I'd put project_number as "P229560-3"? That's the evaluation report number. Actually let me put test_reports: [{id: "P229560-3", role: "evaluation_report"}]. project_number — I could omit or use "P229560-3". I'll use project_number: "P229560-3" since it's the LNE project/report number. Hmm, it's labeled "EVALUATION REPORT". Better to put it in test_reports and leave project_number out. Actually it could serve as both. I'll put it in test_reports only.

- page_total: The certificate says annex consists of 7 pages. Total document pages = 8 (1 cert + 7 annex). page_total probably refers to the total pages of the document/certificate. The statement "7 page(s)" refers to annex. I'd say page_total: 7 (annex pages)... Hmm. "The principal characteristics are set out in the appendix hereto, which forms part of the OIML certificate of conformity and consists of 7 page(s)." I think page_total should reflect the document's total pages = 8. But the certificate explicitly says 7 pages. The certificate page count typically includes annex. Since PDF has 8 pages (page 1 + 7 annex pages), page_total: 8? The field meaning: "page_total" for the document-level certificate. I'll go with 7 since the certificate says 7 page(s)... but the actual PDF is 8 pages. Hmm. The certificate itself (1 page) + annex (7 pages) = 8 total. The phrase "consists of 7 page(s)" refers to the annex. I think page_total = 8 for the whole document. But to be safe, use the explicit statement? The instruction says don't fabricate; the document explicitly says the annex is 7 pages. The field is "page_total" without more specificity. I'll use 7 since that's what the document explicitly states about the certificate's page composition... Actually let me think about the intent: page_total likely describes the total number of pages of the certificate document (which would be 8 here including the main page). Given ambiguity, I'll go with 7 as explicitly stated — no wait. Hmm.

The certificate document = page 1 + annex 7 pages = 8 pages. The explicit statement "7 page(s)" is about the annex. The schema field is document-level "page_total". I'll go with 7 because that's the only explicit number given in the document. Either choice is defensible; I'll pick 7 with the annex interpretation... Actually, many extraction pipelines use page_total for the whole certificate file. The whole file has 8 pages. But I only know that from the markdown "# Page 1" through "# Page 8". That's evidence too. Total pages in the PDF = 8. I'll use 8.

Hmm, let me reconsider: "The principal characteristics are set out in the appendix hereto, which forms part of the OIML certificate of conformity and consists of 7 page(s)." — This says the certificate of conformity consists of 7 pages (the appendix is part of the certificate). So the certificate = 1 + 7 = 8 pages? Or does "consists of 7 pages" refer to the appendix? Grammatically, "the appendix ... consists of 7 pages". So appendix = 7 pages. Total certificate = 8 pages. I'll use page_total: 8.

- member_state: "FRANCE"
- date_issued: "2023-03-28"
- oiml_issuer_id: not explicitly given. There's no issuer ID number in the markdown (some certs have an authority ID like "7" for NMi). Omit.

issuing_authority:
- name: "Laboratoire National de Métrologie et d'Essais"
- address_lines: ["1, rue Gaston Boissier", "75724 Paris Cedex 15"] — from footer: "Siège social : 1, rue Gaston Boissier - 75724 Paris Cedex 15". This is the address.
- person_responsible: "Emeric MOREL"
- person_title: "Head of Instrumentation Certification Department" (Responsable du Département Certification Instrumentation)
- phone: "01 40 43 37 00" — from footer. Could normalize to "+33 1 40 43 37 00" but don't fabricate; keep "01 40 43 37 00".
- email: "info@lne.fr"
- website: "lne.fr" or "www.lne.fr"? The text says "lne.fr". Use "lne.fr". Also cofrac "www.cofrac.fr" is accreditation scope, not LNE website. I'll use "lne.fr".
- oiml_issuer_id: omit (not present).

applicants:
- name: "DIEHL METERING GMBH", address_lines: ["Industriestrasse 13", "91522 Ansbach", "GERMANY"] — the markdown says "DIEHL METERING GMBH - Industriestrasse 13 / GERMANY 91522 ANSBACH". So address: Industriestrasse 13, 91522 Ansbach, Germany.

manufacturers:
- name: "DIEHL METERING GMBH", address_lines: ["Industriestrasse 13", "91522 Ansbach", "Germany"]

certified_type:
- category: "Water meter"
- type_designations: ["174"]
- module_designation: Not applicable? Not mentioned. Omit or null. I'll omit... schema includes module_designation; for water meters not relevant. I'll set null? The rule: don't fabricate. I'll omit the key.
- description: "Water meter type 174" — the identification. Could put description: "Water meter for cold potable water and hot water, type 174". Keep simple: "Water meter type 174".

model_family:
- family_name: "174"? The type is 174 and variants are by nominal diameter. family_name: "174" seems reasonable. Or null. I'll use "174".
- models: DN50, DN65, DN80, DN100, DN125, DN150, DN200. model_id: "DN50" etc. attributes could include connections and lengths per model. Actually per-model attributes: connections, lengths. I can put attributes: {"nominal_diameter_mm": 50} etc. Hmm, attributes{} is free-form. But the model_level characteristics matrix will capture per-model values. Let me define models with attributes containing connections and lengths:

```
{"model_id": "DN50", "attributes": {"connections": ["Flange DN50", "Rotable flange DN50"], "lengths_mm": [200, 270, 300]}}
```

Hmm, lengths are config-level options, not single values. Maybe attributes: {"connection_types": "Flange DN50 / Rotable flange DN50", "lengths": "200 mm ; 270 mm ; 300 mm"}. Keep it simple: strings for these attribute values, or put in matrix_tables.

Actually, let me think about how to best structure the whole characteristics data.

The certificate covers 7 models (by DN). Per-model varying attributes:
- nominal_diameter (mm): 50, 65, 80, 100, 125, 150, 200
- q3 (m³/h): 25, 40, 63, 100, 160, 250, 400
- q4 (m³/h): 31.25, 50, 78.75, 125, 200, 312.5, 500
- connection types: Flange DNxx / Rotable flange DNxx (DN125, DN150, DN200 only flange)
- lengths (mm): vary per model (lists)
- indicating_range (m³): 99999 (DN50, DN65), 999999 (rest)
- verification_scale_interval (dm³): 0.01 (DN50, DN65), 0.1 (rest)
- temperature range availability: DN50–DN125 support 30/50/70/90°C; DN150/DN200 only 30/50°C.

Constant attributes (type_level):
- body: "Iron cast coated / Stainless steel"
- indicating device: "Plastic"
- q2/q1: 1.6 (dimensionless)
- maximum admissible pressure: 10/16 bar → value {min:10, max:16}, unit "bar"
- pressure loss class: "Δp16"
- accuracy class: 2
- environmental class: "B / O"
- climatic influence class: -25…55 °C → value {min:-25, max:55}, unit "°C"
- electromagnetic influence class: "E1 / E2"
- measurement of reverse flow: "No (the meter can withstand accidental reverse flow without deterioration or change in its metrological properties for forward flow)"
- software identification: "001.000.008; Checksum CRC: 0h1003"

Per-configuration attributes (temperature × installation position):
- q3/q1 ratio depends on (model, temperature range option, installation position). This is a multi-dimensional table: model × temperature (4 options for ≤DN125, 2 for ≥DN150) × position (horizontal, vertical/rise/down/45°).

How to represent? Options:
1. matrix_tables[]: one table per model (7 tables) replicating the annex tables.
2. model_level entries: q3_q1_ratio_horizontal and q3_q1_ratio_vertical with values per model being strings like "40-1000".

The q3/q1 values are lists of possible ratios (R-value selections): e.g., for DN50 horizontal T30: 40,50,63,80,100,125,160,200,250,315,400,500,630,800,1000. These are the possible Q3/Q1 ratio values for that configuration. So the "value" is a list of numbers.

The schema's structured value allows value: number | {min,max} | string. A list isn't in there. Hmm. But we could represent as string "40–1000 (R40 to R1000)"? Or as a string listing. Alternatively represent as {min: 40, max: 1000}? That loses the discrete steps but is a fair compact representation? Actually the meaning: the meter type is approved for Q3/Q1 ratios chosen from the R10 series between 40 and 1000. The min/max representation {min: 40, max: 1000} captures the range. But it loses discreteness. Hmm.

The schema says value can be number | {min,max} | string. For safety, I could keep as a string of comma/hyphen separated values: "40,50,63,80,100,125,160,200,250,315,400,500,630,800,1000". That's a list-as-string which is allowed? The rules say lists of values (like Emax list) are model matrices, not list-as-value. But here it's a set of allowed configuration options, a genuinely list-valued attribute.

I think the cleanest: matrix_tables with one entry per model capturing the full table including columns: indicating_device? No — keep to varying fields.

Let me design matrix_tables: name: "Metrology characteristics by nominal diameter (Annex)". columns: ["model", "nominal_diameter", "q3", "q4", "connection", "lengths", "indicating_range", "verification_scale_interval", "temperature_ranges"]... This is getting big but preserves data.

Alternatively: matrix_tables per temperature/position for q3/q1.

Given the layered schema, I'll do:

1. model_family.models with model_id "DN50" ... "DN200", attributes containing connection and length options.

2. characteristics.type_level for constant attributes.

3. characteristics.model_level for: nominal_diameter, q3, q4, indicating_range, verification_scale_interval.

4. characteristics.config_level for q3/q1 ratio: axis "temperature_range_and_installation_position". Values: condition strings like "DN50, water 0.1–30 °C, horizontal" → value "40–1000 (R40 series)". Hmm.

Actually config_level entries: {attribute, axis, values: [{condition, value}]}. The value follows structured form with {condition, value, unit_symbol}. So I can do:

```
{
  "attribute": "q3_q1_ratio",
  "axis": "model × water_temperature_range × installation_position",
  "values": [
    {"condition": "DN50 | 0.1–30 °C | horizontal", "value": "40–1000"},
    ...
  ]
}
```

That's a lot of entries: 7 models × up to 4 temps × 2 positions = 50 entries for ≤DN125 (5 models × 4 temps × 2 = 40) + 2 models × 2 temps × 2 = 8, total 48 entries. That's verbose but accurate.

Alternatively use matrix_tables: one table "Q3/Q1 ratio options by model, temperature and installation position" with columns model, temperature_range, horizontal, vertical. 7 models × up to 4 temps = 5*4 + 2*2 = 24 rows. That's more compact and preserves the table structure. And the schema says matrix_tables preserve multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere. I think using matrix_tables for the q3/q1 tables is right, and also possibly a model summary table.

Let me structure:

matrix_tables:
1. name: "Metrology characteristics by nominal diameter"
   columns: ["model", "nominal_diameter_mm", "q3_m3_h", "q4_m3_h", "connections", "connection_lengths_mm", "indicating_range_m3", "verification_scale_interval_dm3"]
   rows: 7 rows.

Hmm, but I'm also putting these in model_level. Duplication is fine per the R137 example (both matrix_tables AND model_level). OK.

2. name: "Q3/Q1 ratio options by model, water temperature and installation position"
   columns: ["model", "water_temperature_range", "q3_q1_horizontal", "q3_q1_vertical_rise_pipe_down_pipe_angle_45"]
   rows: 24 rows.

Also could include temperature_range table:
3. name: "Water temperature ranges by model"
   columns: ["model", "ranges"]
   rows...

Or handle temperature ranges in config_level: attribute "water_temperature_range", values per model: {condition: "DN50", value: "0.1–30 / 0.1–50 / 0.1–70 / 0.1–90 °C"}. Actually this is a list of options per model. I'll put in model_level as attribute "water_temperature_range_options" with string values per model: "0.1–30 °C; 0.1–50 °C; 0.1–70 °C; 0.1–90 °C" for DN50–DN125, and "0.1–30 °C; 0.1–50 °C" for DN150/DN200. Hmm, unit extraction: values are ranges; keep as strings given multiple options. Or as value: "0,1 to 30" etc. Let me use value strings like "0.1 to 30 °C; 0.1 to 50 °C; 0.1 to 70 °C; 0.1 to 90 °C" with unit_symbol "°C"? That has unit embedded. Alternatively value: "0.1–30; 0.1–50; 0.1–70; 0.1–90", unit_symbol: "°C". That's cleaner.

Now the temperature ranges themselves: "0,1 to 30" → min 0.1, max 30. Four options. The temperature range option axis: T30, T50, T70, T90 (standard designations). Could do config_level: attribute "water_temperature_range", axis "model", values: [{condition: "DN50", value: ...}]. Eh.

Hmm wait — should value be "40–1000" as {min:40, max:1000}? The values are discrete: 40,50,63,80,100,125,160,200,250,315,400,500,630,800,1000. These are R10 series preferred numbers. As {min: 40, max: 1000} would suggest continuity. As string "40, 50, 63, 80, 100, 125, 160, 200, 250, 315, 400, 500, 630, 800, 1000" preserves exactly. The rule "Lists of values" concerns a single attribute varying across models → model matrix. Here it's the set of permitted ratios for a given configuration — a list-valued attribute. I'll keep them as strings of comma-separated numbers to be faithful. Hmm, but rules say convert "25,30,50..." lists to model matrices — that's when it indicates model variants. Actually, wait. Let me reconsider: maybe represent as value string "40–1000" — no, I'll use full lists for fidelity. Hmm, it's 15 numbers for some cells. Fine.
